subject: BlueCrest renewal — model affinity + KV cache persistence prioritization
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@bluecresthealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-08T10:14:00-08:00
Subject: BlueCrest renewal — model affinity + KV cache persistence prioritization

Team — quick summary and an ask: BlueCrest (Alex, cc'd) is at signature if we can commit to two platform items by their renewal and we will close +12m reserved capacity: (1) model affinity/sticky routing for tenant X to avoid cold model swaps under burst and (2) persistent KV cache per tenant so their conversational state doesn't fall back to cold-warm on every failover.

Why: in our last POC they hit 800–1k QPS peaks during claims ingestion windows; latency spikes and a few inference mismatches due to model mismatch have been called out in the security/ops review. Procurement said these two items are gating the final sign-off.

Asks: can Product/Eng triage and give a feasible scope + minimal acceptance criteria by EOD Thursday? Attached: BC NDA redline and an MVP spec (high level).

Renewal timeline: DocuSign to vendor legal by 2026-12-20; customer expects capability preview by 2027-01-20.

Thanks — Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Exec, Redwood Inference
attachments: BC_NDA_redline.pdf; MVP_spec_kv-cache.md

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@bluecresthealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-09T09:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: BlueCrest renewal — model affinity + KV cache persistence prioritization

Thanks Vanessa — looping in Product/Platform notes and initial read:

Short answer: both capabilities are doable but with clear tradeoffs. High-level Qs to size the work:
- Target steady QPS and peak concurrency (their POC numbers help; Vanessa, can you confirm 1k QPS peak and expected sustained 200–300 QPS?)
- Is their requirement for strict tenant-level KV durability (survive host restarts) or is in-memory warm-pool enough?
- Any hard latency SLOs (p50/p95) the customer will refuse?

Initial technical comments:
- Model affinity: we can implement sticky routing at the routing layer with per-tenant model pins and a fallback policy. This is mostly routing + config + small runtime guards (safe). Risk: reduces load balancing flexibility during skews.
- Persistent KV cache: more complex — we'd need a per-tenant backing store (Redis with TTLs or local persistence to fast NVMe). If they need cross-host durability during failover, it's a nontrivial infra addition and will add cost and operational surface area.

Proposal: scope an MVP that does (A) per-tenant model pin config + enforced runtime pin check, and (B) a best-effort KV warm-cache persisted to a Redis cluster with TTL-based eviction — labeled as "durable enough for POC". Delivery estimate: scoped spike + design in 2 sprints (4 weeks) and engineering rollout in 3 more sprints depending on infra availability.

I'll put a short PRD bullet list together today if you confirm QPS and the durability ask.

—Irene 
Irene Choi
Senior PM, Platform

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@bluecresthealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-10T11:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: BlueCrest renewal — model affinity + KV cache persistence prioritization

On Wed, Dec 9, 2026 at 09:21 AM Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Initial technical comments...

Quick engineering readout and proposed plan from infra side:

Summary: we can deliver a minimal, low-risk path that meets BlueCrest's stated needs for the renewal preview window if Product narrows acceptance criteria now. Recommended approach:
1) Model affinity: implement per-tenant model pinning in the router with a transparent fallback to a compatible model family. No runtime binary change required beyond a small router flag + config API. Estimate: 3 engineer-weeks (1 engineer, part time) for implementation + tests.
2) KV cache persistence MVP: use managed Redis cluster scoped to the tenant with strict TTLs + write-through from the runtime on token commit. This avoids local NVMe complexity and meets "survive host restart" requirement if we replicate. Estimate: 6 engineer-weeks (1.5 engineers) to wire, secure (auth/TLS), and add eviction/monitoring hooks.

Risks & tradeoffs:
- Memory/storage cost increase and per-tenant Redis billing: we should price this into the reserved capacity.
- Observability: we'll need tracing hooks and per-tenant hit/miss dashboards — add one sprint to backlog for ops dashboards.

Acceptance criteria suggestion (please confirm):
- Model affinity: configured tenant pin ensures p95 inference latency does not degrade more than 10% vs baseline under identical load.
- KV persistence: cache survives process restart with >90% hit recovery for recent sessions; measured in a 30-minute post-failover window.

If Sales can commit to a 12-month reserved capacity (BC-2026-42) and pay for the additional infra tag, we can prioritize this as a high-impact sprint slot. Otherwise we scope to experimental EAP only. Vanessa — can you confirm the commercial ask/commit? Alex — any pushback on Redis approach?

—Ben
Ben Carter
Engineering Lead, Inference Runtime

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@bluecresthealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-12T16:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: BlueCrest renewal — model affinity + KV cache persistence prioritization

Thanks all for the fast replies. Vanessa — pushing this to close is high priority; BlueCrest is strategic.

Decision: product approves a narrowed MVP as Ben outlined (model pin + Redis-backed KV with replication and TTL). Constraints:
- Scope limit: no NVMe local persistence in MVP; we will revisit after renewal.
- Delivery window: preview by 2027-01-20 with production-ready work targeted by end of Q1 2027.
- Product must provide a short PRD (Irene) with acceptance criteria by 2026-12-15 and a rollout plan including a canary and rollback steps.

Commercial trade: Sales commits to 12-month reserved capacity (BC-2026-42) with an infra uplift. Vanessa — please update the HubSpot record and confirm the uplift percentage; attach signed DocuSign by 2026-12-20. I put a DocuSign link in the HubSpot note for convenience.

Alex — appreciate collaboration; we will schedule a technical sync next week to align on SLA measurements.

Monica Patel
VP, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
